## Implementation

Flag: STRATA_DECODE_SERVICE_CPU=1 (exact value 1 only). Separate from STRATA_DECODE_TIMING, STRATA_DECODE_ROUTE_LEDGER and STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE. The latter must stay off: it changes the eligible DF branch. No existing flag semantics changed.

Request scope is created beside the bounded ledger in the ordinary decode block; it inherits the ordinary/no-batch/single-stage/no-MTP/no-suffix/no-lookup eligibility. Capacity is raw verifier capacity, not NT. Actual dispatch NT=1 is independently enforced as a diagnostic condition. Native layout, matching layer count <=64, no remote experts and <=128 workers bound collection; ineligibility emits one incomplete request receipt without changing inference selection. Model 48 layers/512 experts/K10/raw spec4 is within this diagnostic envelope, but only observed NT/coverage can establish that a run actually fits it.

Issuer scopes cover the complete per-layer `expert_pool_dispatch_multi` callback, including route/activation/job planning and its existing pool call, final accounting and failure returns. They do not change routing/planning eligibility. The request binding is guarded by one host-only mutex; each request has one host-only mutex held by the issuer for the existing complete callback. These do not participate in worker claims. No new explicit atomics are added. Shared ownership uses standard host shared_ptr lifetime/reference counting, never device state.

Pool storage is fixed <=65536 bytes (static_assert), 129 single-writer cache-aligned slots: issuer slot0 and worker id+1. No worker writes another slot or global validity state. Each direct native_gu_rows/native_quant_h/native_down_rows invocation/range has a pair of CPU reads and steady-clock endpoints. Existing Q2 GU+up+SwiGLU range, ActQ intermediate quantization and Q2 Down branches have separate fallback buckets, so common IQ layers with Q2 Down do not silently lose CPU work. Q2 GU counts one range including two existing q2_rows_any invocations plus SwiGLU; it is explicitly not a direct native_gu_rows call. Direct native ranges have one scope each, not per-row clocks. Worker quant buckets stay zero because quant is already issued on the caller. Counts separate claimed row tasks from invocation/ranges; one task can span experts.

Issuer GU/Down phase counters bracket existing parked-before, begin_batch/publish-through-wait_done, and done-through-final-wait_parked boundaries. The calls remain in their original order, with the same scheduling/work partition and no new GPU events, copies, waits, device branches or profiling flags. Intermediate quant is call-scoped on the issuer. Request decode_wall_ms reuses the existing measurement before final wait_commit; diagnostic formatting is after that measurement.

## Timing domains and overlap

Linux CPU time is CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, for the thread actually executing the call. Non-Linux returns unavailable without substituting process CPU time. Every attempted call scope retains calls and two attempted CPU reads even when either read fails; failed/reversed reads make it incomplete, and accumulation/merge are checked for saturation. The close availability probe contributes one separately declared attempted CPU read. CPU read attempts are instrumentation counts, not measured overhead.

Per-call wall is a steady-clock interval; worker wall sum is labelled call_worker_sum, not elapsed time. Issuer callback wall contains phase wall and inline call wall; phase wall can overlap GPU execution. Worker call CPU excludes worker park loops and claim/setup outside ranges. Issuer callback CPU includes its existing host work/spins and inline native calls. Phase boundaries cover existing synchronization and host drain. Summing CPU across distinct workers is service consumption; adding overlapping wall spans, worker wall, request wall or GPU ticks is invalid. wall minus same-thread CPU is residual/blocked-or-preempted, not pure wait. No verifier ring/flag/window timeline or GPU completion clock was added; this diagnostic alone cannot establish GPU overlap or critical path.

## Synchronization and lifetime proof (source reasoning only)

Binding exists before the first layer. Dispatch retrieves shared state under the binding mutex, then locks only that request. Native pool service pointer is set by the existing serialized issuer before batch publication. Worker diagnostics are accessed only after claim succeeds; existing head.store(release), epoch publication and claim acquire/acq_rel expose the pointer/state. A late worker failing its epoch claim never reads the pointer. Each call's clock/counter scope ends before existing done_.fetch_add(release); worker slot writes precede existing parked_.fetch_add(acq_rel). After native run returns through final wait_parked(acquire), callback destruction clears the pointer, then destroys the callback clock while still holding request lock. No worker-counter reads or output occurs until request close obtains that lock after observer removal. A callback already holding shared state at removal either finishes first or observes active=false and records nothing; normal coverage then decides completeness. Existing normal close waits final verify commit first. Strong references preserve state during early close; stack guards unbind on ordinary exception/return. Abort/kill may prevent any close receipt and is never a completed result. This proof assumes the pool's existing single-issuer contract; no unsupported concurrent issuer is introduced or repaired.

A complete receipt requires ordinary length/stop close, nonnegative emitted count, each layer's completed callback count and valid call clock receipts matching emitted, all worker/phase clocks valid, task sums equal planned tasks, phase-clock counts equal across the three boundaries, each task having at least one matching GU/Down call-range receipt, intermediate quant call count matching CPU jobs, and no overflow in counters/aggregates. Partial samples remain visible with incomplete=1. Diagnostic status preserves the original close status, including formatting/allocation failure. The final close row is authoritative.

One CPU-service close block <=65536 bytes, no perjob/perrow log or unbounded history. Allocation failure/ineligible request emits a single short incomplete receipt. Full state is request-local and reset by creating a fresh request object. Exact issuer/worker task counts and call counts are reported, per-layer callback receipts and phase aggregates are bounded. Existing inherited D ledger remains a separate complementary owner/NT/call coverage diagnostic; its output budget remains 512KiB, so the combined independently enabled diagnostics do not share a 64KiB total budget. CPU-service output itself has the requested 64KiB cap. Logical ledger bytes are never converted to physical traffic or time.

## Off path

When off, request scope takes no allocation and returns without output. Dispatcher observer returns before locking or copying a live observer, and all clock scopes receive nullptr. Pool instrumentation performs conditional null checks only, and no diagnostic clock reads, perjob allocation, counter writes, new atomic instructions or extra output are requested. Added object fields: one empty shared_ptr per ExpertDispatch and one null pointer per ExpertPool; class scope/branch overhead is not claimed zero and needs Main's off/on performance comparison. Existing flags and math/sampler/cache/workpartition/pool scheduling remain unchanged by source inspection.

## Fixture and validation not executed

New fixture tools/test_decode_service_budget.cpp covers exact injected clock accounting, null-scope hotOFF with 10000 scopes and zero injected CPU/wall reads, failure/reversal/incomplete receipts, normal versus failure coverage, emitted mismatch, missing reads, CPU/wall/count/read overflow, merge, reset, exception scope unwind, actual parallel threads writing distinct slots with aggregation only after joins, native availability behavior, worker bounds, missing tasks and task overflow. It asserts but has not run; Main must preserve assertions with -UNDEBUG. New pure counter header depends on standard host libraries only; fixture needs no GPU/native weights. No CMake target was added; commands compile the fixture directly.

Enable STRATA_DECODE_SERVICE_CPU only in diagnostic arm; optionally run complementary D route coverage with its own explicitly recorded overhead. Record independent samples at 16K/32K (as authorized by Main), output/token/logit equivalence, original failure status, normal completion, allcall/task/layer checks, clock read attempts, decode wall and instrumentation overhead. No overhead or performance result is inferred here. Any later GPU profiling belongs to a separately configured pass because its eligible branch differs.
